sentences.text: ---- Applicant  Versus   State Of Chhattisgarh Through The Station House Officer, Police  Station Kota, District- Bilaspur, Chhattisgarh
---- Respondent For Applicant : Ms. Maya Chaturvijani, Advocate For State : Mr. R. C. S. Deo, Panel Lawyer Hon'ble Shri Justice Parth Prateem Sahu Order On Board 11/06/2024 1.
Applicant has filed this second bail application under Section 439 of CrPC for grant of regular bail.

First bail application was dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to repeat the prayer after examination of victim.
2.

Applicant was arrested in connection with Crime No. 69 of 2024 registered at Police Station Kota,
District - Bilaspur for offence punishable under Section 376 of I.P.C. and Section 4, 6 of POCSO Act,
2012.
3. Pursuant to notice issued, parents of victim appeared before this Court through virtual mode from DLSA Bilaspur and submitted that they are having no objection in grant of bail to applicant.
4. Learned counsel for applicant submits that applicant is innocent, Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:18633 he has not committed any offence as alleged.
He has been falsely implicated in the aforementioned crime.

After withdrawl of first bail application on 27.03.2024, victim has now Raj Manikpuri vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/125435995/
1 been examined before learned Trial Court and she has not supported the case of prosecution.

entities.text: Raj Manikpuri vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Applicant is in jail since 20.01.2024, hence, he may be enlarged on bail.
5.

Learned State counsel opposes the submission made by learned counsel for applicant and submits that specific allegation is levelled against applicant in the statement of victim recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C.
He further submits that deposition of victim which has been relied upon by learned counsel for applicant is subject matter of appreciation by learned Trial Court.
6. I have heard learned counsel for the parties.

7. Taking into consideration facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegation, submission of learned counsel for the parties, in particular, submission of learned counsel for applicant based on deposition of victim as also submission of parents of victim, without commenting anything on merits of the case, I am inclined to enlarge the applicant on bail.
8.
Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on regular bail, upon furnishing a bail bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/- with one surety in the like sum to the satisfaction of the Court on the conditions that - Neutral Citation 2024:CGHC:18633 a) Applicant shall appear before the Trial Court regularly on each and every date, unless exempted from appearance.
b) The applicant shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
c) If the applicant is found involved in similar offence in future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of Bail.
Certified copy as per rules.

Sd/-
 (Parth Prateem Sahu)
